title: TikTok Explores Peer-to-Peer Payments via Direct Messages
summary: TikTok is reportedly developing a feature to enable peer-to-peer (P2P) payments through direct messages (DMs) using its existing TikTok Pay system. References to the feature were discovered in the code of TikTok’s U.S. iPhone app, suggesting early-stage development. The feature would allow users to send money with accompanying messages, similar to Venmo. TikTok has not confirmed testing or a release timeline. This move aligns with TikTok’s broader expansion into financial services, including an application to operate as a fintech company in Brazil. Other social platforms like X (formerly Twitter) are also venturing into P2P payments.
key_points: TikTok is developing a P2P payments feature via DMs, leveraging its TikTok Pay system already used in Southeast Asia for TikTok Shop.
The feature was discovered in the code of TikTok’s U.S. iPhone app, indicating early development stages.
Users would be able to 'tap to accept' payments and include messages, similar to Venmo’s functionality.
TikTok stated the feature is not currently being tested, and no release timeline has been confirmed.
This initiative follows TikTok’s broader push into financial services, including an application to operate as a fintech company in Brazil.
TikTok’s expansion mirrors trends in social media platforms (e.g., X’s X Money) integrating financial services.
